questions.question: What is choreography?
choices: The composition and organization of movement for a dance

questions.question: A choreographer repeats a short movement idea throughout a dance. What is this idea often called?
Which structure has two contrasting sections, A and B?
What is ABA form?
choices: Three unrelated dances performed at once
A line of dancers moving in canon
A rhythm with three beats only
A section returns after a contrasting middle section

questions.question: A movement phrase is performed by one dancer, then repeated by others at different times. What device is used?
Why might a choreographer vary a repeated motif?
choices: To develop an idea while helping the audience recognize its transformation
To change the dance's genre automatically

questions.question: A dance moves from a solo to a group formation. What compositional element changes?
choices: Number of performers and spatial relationship

questions.question: What can a transition do in choreography?
choices: Remove the need for a beginning
Connect sections and guide the shift in movement or focus

questions.question: A choreographer selects a circular pathway for a reunion scene. What can this choice communicate?
choices: A sense of connection or gathering, depending on context
One fixed meaning in every dance

questions.question: Which choice is an example of contrast in choreography?
choices: Repeating the same speed and level

questions.question: How can a choreographer use unison?
choices: Stagger the same phrase across dancers
Ask each dancer to perform unrelated material
Coordinate dancers to perform the same movement at the same time

questions.question: A group dance begins in a scattered formation and ends in a tight cluster. What might the change help show?
choices: A development in relationships or focus

questions.question: Why should choreographers consider transitions when arranging sections?
choices: Transitions help the dance feel connected and intentional
Transitions are only for costume changes

questions.question: What is one way to develop a movement motif?
choices: Repeat it exactly and never vary it
Change its level, direction, timing, or energy while retaining a recognizable feature
Replace it with an unrelated costume

questions.question: A choreographer wants the audience to notice a particular dancer. Which choice could help?
choices: Place all dancers in identical positions
Use spacing, focus, or contrasting movement to draw attention
Turn the lights off for the entire dance

questions.question: What does improvisation contribute to some choreography processes?
choices: It can generate movement material for later selection and organization

questions.question: Why is rehearsal important during choreography development?
choices: It reveals how movement, timing, spacing, and transitions work in practice
It removes the need for communication
It guarantees every performance is identical

questions.question: A choreographer sets a movement phrase to a musical accent. What relationship is being shaped?
A dance has a clear opening, development, and ending. What does this demonstrate?
What is the strongest way to evaluate whether a choreographic choice works?
choices: Count only how many steps it contains
Ask whether it is the hardest movement
Consider its effect on the dance's idea, movement, and audience experience
